Benjamin Graham (1894-1976), padre dell': Benjamin Graham (1894-1976), the father of security analysis and Buffett's teacher; ran Graham-Newman Corporation from 1936 to 1956.
The Intelligent Investor (1949), i crite: The Intelligent Investor (1949), the criteria for the defensive investor.
Azienda grande; current ratio almeno 2;: A large company; current ratio of at least 2; positive earnings in each of the last 10 years; uninterrupted dividends for 20 years; earnings per share up by at least one third over 10 years; P/E of at most 15 on 3-year average earnings; P/E x P/B of at most 22.5.
Utili e dividendi: 5 esercizi di fila in: Earnings and dividends: 5 consecutive fiscal years instead of 10 and 20 (SEC data starts in 2009); minimum growth of 3% a year over 5 fiscal years (one third over 10 years); P/E on the trailing 12 months, not on the 3-year average. Financials and Utilities excluded: the current ratio means nothing for them (Graham had separate criteria). Ranked by P/E x P/B, rebalanced annually.
Aziende solide, con utili e dividendi co: Sound companies with steady earnings and dividends, bought at a moderate price relative to earnings and book value. If only a few pass, the rest stays in cash.
Lettere agli azionisti di Berkshire Hath: Berkshire Hathaway shareholder letters; R. Hagstrom, The Warren Buffett Way (1994).
Un'azienda che capisce, con un vantaggio: A business he understands, with a durable competitive advantage: high ROE for many years without too much debt, predictable and growing earnings, honest and capable management, bought below its value ("owner earnings", i.e. the cash it generates for its owners).
ROE minimo degli ultimi 5 esercizi almen: Minimum ROE over the last 5 fiscal years of at least 15%, net debt of at most 2 years of EBITDA, earnings per share growing at least 5% a year and no losses in the last 5 fiscal years; ranked by free cash flow yield (the "owner earnings") and average ROIC. All the judgment is missing: competitive advantage, management, understanding the business. Financials and Utilities excluded (Buffett owns them: banks, insurers, energy) because their debt ratios are not comparable.
Redditività alta e costante, poco debito: High and consistent profitability, little debt, growing earnings; among these, the ones that generate the most cash relative to price. Few stocks, held for the long term.
Charlie Munger (1924-2023), socio di Buf: Charlie Munger (1924-2023), Buffett's partner at Berkshire Hathaway; before that, his own investment partnership (1962-1975).
Discorsi raccolti in Poor Charlie's Alma: Speeches collected in Poor Charlie's Almanack (2005).
\"Un'azienda meravigliosa a un prezzo eq: "A wonderful company at a fair price is better than a fair company at a wonderful price": very few companies of the highest quality, with a durable advantage, held for decades.
ROIC medio degli ultimi 5 esercizi almen: Average ROIC over the last 5 fiscal years of at least 20%, gross margin of at least 40%, little debt, always profitable; ranked half on ROIC and half on free cash flow yield (the fair price); 12 stocks, rebalanced once a year (Munger hardly ever sold). The judgment on competitive advantage is missing.
Le aziende con il rendimento sul capital: The companies with the highest and most consistent return on capital, high margins and little debt; a concentrated portfolio.
Peter Lynch (1944), gestore del fondo Fi: Peter Lynch (1944), manager of the Fidelity Magellan fund from 1977 to 1990.
One Up on Wall Street (1989), Beating th: One Up on Wall Street (1989), Beating the Street (1993).
P/E non più alto della crescita degli ut: P/E no higher than the earnings growth rate (PEG below 1, better below 0.5); 20-25% growth is ideal, above 50% is suspect; little debt; inventories not growing faster than sales; know the company and its "story".
PEG = P/E degli ultimi 12 mesi / crescit: PEG = trailing 12-month P/E / annual growth of earnings per share over 5 fiscal years; growth between 10 and 50%; debt/equity of at most 0.8; the 30 with the lowest PEG, every quarter. The inventory check and the "story" are missing. Lynch found many ideas among small companies, outside the S&P 500.
Aziende che crescono tra il 10 e il 50%: Companies growing 10 to 50% a year, with little debt, priced below their growth rate (PEG below 1).
Philip A. Fisher (1907-2004), Fisher & C: Philip A. Fisher (1907-2004), Fisher & Co. from 1931 to 1999; one of the first growth investors.
Common Stocks and Uncommon Profits (1958: Common Stocks and Uncommon Profits (1958), the 15 points.
Prodotti con un mercato in crescita per: Products with a market that keeps growing for years, effective research and development, high and improving margins, a good sales organization, capable and honest management, no dilutive equity issues. Information gathered by talking to customers, suppliers and competitors.
Ricavi in crescita di almeno l'8% l'anno: Revenue growing at least 8% a year over 5 fiscal years, operating margin in the better half of its sector and higher than three years earlier, R&D spending of at least 2% of revenue (companies that do not report it are left out), share count up by at most 2% in a year; rebalanced annually. Almost all the qualitative work of the 15 points is missing.
Aziende con ricavi in crescita da anni,: Companies with revenue growing for years, margins above their sector and rising, that invest in research and do not dilute shareholders. Held for the long term.
Sir John Templeton (1912-2008), Templeto: Sir John Templeton (1912-2008), Templeton Growth Fund since 1954.
Interviste e scritti raccolti in The Tem: Interviews and writings collected in The Templeton Touch (2012) and Investing the Templeton Way (2008).
Comprare nel momento di massimo pessimis: Buy at the point of maximum pessimism: companies whose price has fallen far below their value, comparing the P/E with the company's own history and with the alternatives, worldwide.
P/E di oggi al massimo il 70% della medi: Today's P/E at most 70% of the median of its P/E at the last 5 fiscal year-ends, P/E in the cheaper half of the index, debt/equity of at most 1, profitable in the last 3 fiscal years; the 30 furthest below their own history, every six months. Templeton searched worldwide: here only the S&P 500.
Aziende sane che costano molto meno del: Healthy companies that cost much less than usual relative to their own earnings, and less than the market.
John Neff (1931-2019), Vanguard Windsor: John Neff (1931-2019), Vanguard Windsor Fund from 1964 to 1995.
P/E basso; crescita degli utili tra il 7: Low P/E; earnings growth between 7 and 20% (no more: too expensive and fragile); a dividend; "total return" (growth + dividend) divided by the P/E as high as possible, ideally twice the market's.
P/E nel 40% più basso dell'indice, cresc: P/E in the cheapest 40% of the index, annual growth of earnings per share over 5 fiscal years between 7 and 20%, dividend of at least 1.5%; ranked by Neff ratio, 40 stocks, every six months.
Aziende poco care, con crescita moderata: Inexpensive companies with moderate growth and a dividend: the most (growth + dividend) for each point of P/E.
David Dreman (1936), Dreman Value Manage: David Dreman (1936), Dreman Value Management, Kemper-Dreman funds from the 1980s.
Contrarian Investment Strategies: The Ne: Contrarian Investment Strategies: The Next Generation (1998).
Comprare le azioni più impopolari (il 20: Buy the most unpopular stocks (the 20% with the lowest P/E among large companies), as long as they are sound: high current ratio, little debt, ROE and dividend above average; hold them until the P/E returns to normal.
P/E nel 20% più basso dell'indice, curre: P/E in the cheapest 20% of the index, current ratio of at least 1.5, debt/equity of at most 1, ROE of at least 10%; ranked by dividend and earnings yield; 30 stocks, every six months. Banks drop out on their own (no reported current ratio).
Il 20% più economico dell'indice per P/E: The cheapest 20% of the index by P/E, only if financially sound, favoring those that pay higher dividends.
Walter Schloss (1916-2012), allievo di G: Walter Schloss (1916-2012), a student of Graham; ran his own firm from 1955 to about 2000.
Factors Needed to Make Money in the Stoc: Factors Needed to Make Money in the Stock Market (16 rules, 1994).
Prezzo vicino o sotto il patrimonio nett: Price near or below book value, little or no debt, stocks near multi-year lows, many stocks (even 100) for diversification, patience: holding them about 4 years on average. No forecasts, no meetings with management.
P/B nel 20% più basso dell'indice, debit: P/B in the cheapest 20% of the index, debt/equity of at most 0.5, price at most 30% above the 52-week low; ranked by P/B and closeness to the low; 40 stocks, rebalanced once a year. Schloss mostly bought small, little-followed companies: there are few like that in the S&P 500.
Aziende che costano poco rispetto al pat: Companies that are cheap relative to book value, with little debt, near their lows of the year; many stocks, held for the long term.
Comprare solo con un ampio margine di si: Buy only with a wide margin of safety between price and a conservative value; value the company on the cash it generates, not on accounting earnings; avoid losing money before trying to make it; hold cash when nothing is cheap enough.
Free cash flow / enterprise value almeno: Free cash flow / enterprise value of at least 6%, net debt of at most 2.5 years of EBITDA, profitable in the last 3 fiscal years; the 20 with the highest yield, every six months; if fewer pass, the rest stays in cash. Baupost also invests heavily in debt, special situations and private companies.
Le aziende che generano più cassa rispet: The companies that generate the most cash relative to what it costs to buy all of them, debt included, with a conservative balance sheet.
Martin Zweig (1942-2013), Zweig Fund e n: Martin Zweig (1942-2013), Zweig Fund and The Zweig Forecast newsletter.
Utili trimestrali in crescita sostenuta: Quarterly earnings growing steadily and accelerating, revenue growing at least as fast as earnings, P/E no more than 3 times the market's, relative strength of the stock; and above all "don't fight the Fed or the tape": reduced exposure when rates and the market are unfavorable.
Crescita dell'utile dell'ultimo trimestr: Latest-quarter earnings growth of at least 20% and not slowing, revenue +5%, P/E of at most 40, momentum in the better half; 30 stocks every quarter. The market part (rates and trend), which for Zweig decided how much to invest, is missing.
Utili in forte crescita e in accelerazio: Earnings growing strongly and accelerating, growing revenue, a rising price, a P/E that is not excessive.
William O'Neil (1933-2023), fondatore di: William O'Neil (1933-2023), founder of Investor's Business Daily.
How to Make Money in Stocks (1988).
C: utili dell'ultimo trimestre +25% o pi: C: latest-quarter earnings up 25% or more; A: annual earnings up 25% over the last 3 years; N: new products, management or highs; S: supply and demand for the shares; L: sector leader (high relative strength); I: bought by institutional investors; M: market in an uptrend. Sell at once on a 7-8% loss.
C: utile dell'ultimo trimestre +25%; A:: C: latest-quarter earnings +25%; A: earnings per share +15% a year over 5 fiscal years (25% over 3 years would leave very few companies); N: price within 15% of the 52-week high; L: momentum in the top 20%; every month. S, I (the 13Fs of the funds followed are not enough), M and the 7-8% stop-loss are missing: that is the trading part of the method.
Aziende leader: utili trimestrali e annu: Leading companies: quarterly and annual earnings growing strongly, price near its highs and among the strongest in the market.
Richard Driehaus (1942-2021), Driehaus C: Richard Driehaus (1942-2021), Driehaus Capital Management since 1982.
Intervista in J. Schwager, The New Marke: Interview in J. Schwager, The New Market Wizards (1992).
\"Comprare alto e vendere più alto\": ti: "Buy high and sell higher": stocks rising strongly with growing earnings and positive surprises, sold as soon as the story worsens; high turnover.
Momentum nel 20% migliore, utile dell'ul: Momentum in the top 20%, latest-quarter earnings +20% and accelerating; rebalanced monthly. Surprises versus analyst estimates are missing (data not available); Driehaus worked a lot on small companies.
I titoli più forti del mercato, purché g: The strongest stocks in the market, as long as earnings are growing and accelerating. Every month.
James O'Shaughnessy (1960), O'Shaughness: James O'Shaughnessy (1960), O'Shaughnessy Asset Management; a researcher of quantitative strategies.
What Works on Wall Street (1996; Trendin: What Works on Wall Street (1996; Trending Value in the 4th edition, 2011).

Ken Fisher (1950), figlio di Philip Fish: Ken Fisher (1950), son of Philip Fisher, Fisher Investments since 1979.
Super Stocks (1984), dove introduce il r: Super Stocks (1984), where he introduced the price/sales ratio (PSR).
PSR molto basso (sotto 0,75 per le azien: Very low PSR (below 0.75 for industrial companies), growing revenue, low debt, margins that can return to normal: companies in temporary trouble that the market has abandoned.

Terry Smith (1953), Fundsmith Equity Fun: Terry Smith (1953), Fundsmith Equity Fund since 2010.
Lettere annuali di Fundsmith; Investing: Fundsmith annual letters; Investing for Growth (2020).
\"Compra buone aziende, non pagarle trop: "Buy good companies, don't overpay, do nothing": high and consistent return on capital, high gross margins, earnings converted into cash, little debt, growth from reinvestment; no banks, commodities, utilities, autos or airlines.
ROIC medio dei 5 esercizi almeno 15%, ma: Average ROIC over 5 fiscal years of at least 15%, gross margin of at least 40%, operating cash flow at least 90% of net income, net debt of at most 2 years of EBITDA; only the sectors Smith considers (no Financials, Energy, Materials, Utilities, Real Estate); ranked by FCF yield and ROIC; 25 stocks, every year. Jim Slater (1929-2015), investitore e au: Jim Slater (1929-2015), British investor and author.
The Zulu Principle (1992), Beyond the Zu: The Zulu Principle (1992), Beyond the Zulu Principle (1996).

Joel Greenblatt (1957), Gotham Capital d: Joel Greenblatt (1957), Gotham Capital since 1985; professor at Columbia.
